main_result: For the microscopic periodization of a Schwartz test f, Theorem 1 gives convergence of the first m ordinary Haar U(N) moments to Gaussian moments when supp(f̂) ⊆ [−2/m,2/m], with mean ∫f and variance ∫min(|u|,1)|f̂(u)|²du for real f. Theorem 2 takes even real f and gives the corresponding support windows [−1/m,1/m] for Sp(N), with N even, and (−1/m,1/m) for SO(N). Theorem 3 gives exact mixed trace moments under the separate total index bounds N+1 and N−1. Theorem 7 attributes the balanced Fourier cumulant estimate to Soshnikov.

main_result: Theorem 1.1 states convergence of the first m local zero-statistic moments to Gaussian moments, with mean ∫f and variance ∫min(|u|,1)f̂(u)²du, for real even f with f̂∈C_c∞ and supp(f̂)⊂(−2a/m,2a/m). Centers are averaged continuously at H=T^a, 0<a≤1, against a nonnegative mass-one weight w with compact Fourier support in the printed setup. The scaled statistic evaluates the entire extension of f at complex zero ordinates, and the paper does not assume RH. An accompanying scope review examines tail integrability and the sufficient rapidly decreasing subclass.

main_result: Propositions 8–9 give the polynomial-normal density/characteristic function equivalence under the normalized-density or actual-characteristic-function premise, with real location b and symmetric positive-definite precision A. The forward direction transforms a degree-2l polynomial times the nonsingular Gaussian density to a degree-2l polynomial times exp(ibtᵀ−tA⁻¹tᵀ/2). The converse assumes this product is a characteristic function and identifies its polynomial-normal density by Fourier uniqueness. Arbitrary polynomial factors need not give positive-definite transforms.

main_result: For the total zero count of Riemann’s completed xi as a function of t, the opening states an additive O(log T) bound about (T/(2π))log(T/(2π))−T/(2π) for T>28.558, sharpening the additive O(log² T) bound recalled from the same author’s 1895 p. 266. The count is not a count of critical-line zeros alone.
